extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, OPLA/TC staff, patent owners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) involved in reexamination, reissue, interference, or concurrent litigation matters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for handling concurrent ex parte/inter partes reexamination, reissue applications, interferences, and related litigation — including when to merge or stay proceedings, notification requirements, examiner/OPLA roles, and effects of court decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of reexamination request during interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 41.8(a), the patent owner must notify the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences that a request for reexamination was filed, within 20 days of receiving notice of the request having been filed. Where it is the patent owner that files the request for reexamination, the 20 days run from the filing date of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests will be processed in the normal manner. No delay or stay of the reexamination will occur because the requester is not a party to the interference. If the examiner orders reexamination pursuant to 37 CFR 1.525 and subsequently rejects a patent claim corresponding to a count in the interference, the attention of the Board shall be called thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when interference declared while reexamination ongoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.565, the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding before the Office is required to notify the Office when the patent being reexamined becomes involved in an interference by filing in the reexamination proceeding a paper giving notice of the interference proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements of 37 CFR 1.565 and 37 CFR 41.8(a) are designed to keep the Office and appropriate parties informed and, to the extent possible, to eliminate procedural surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to stay reexamination because of interference — timing and propriety
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to stay a reexamination proceeding because of an interference, which is filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) will not be considered, but will be returned to the party submitting the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to stay may be filed by the patent owner as part of the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or subsequent thereto. If a party to the interference other than the patent owner is the requester, that party may petition to stay as part of a reply under 37 CFR 1.535. Any petition by a party who is not the requester is improper under 37 CFR 1.550(g) and will be returned. Petitions filed after the order for reexamination will be referred to OPLA for decision; all merits decisions are made in OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board notification following reexamination certificate amendments/cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims of a patent involved in an interference are canceled or amended by the issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate, the Board must be promptly notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon issuance and publication of the reexamination certificate, the patent owner must notify the administrative patent judge thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy to merge or stay concurrent reissue and ex parte reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and an ex parte reexamination proceeding on which an order pursuant to § 1.525 has been mailed are pending concurrently on a patent, a decision will normally be made to merge the two proceedings or to suspend one of the two proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where merger is ordered, merged examination will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.171 through 1.179 and the patent owner will be required to place and maintain the same claims in the reissue application and the ex parte reexamination during the pendency of the merged proceeding. Examiner actions and patent owner responses in a merged proceeding will apply to both files and be physically entered into both files. Any ex parte reexamination proceeding merged with a reissue application shall be terminated by the grant of the reissued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: General policy against separate concurrent examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy of the Office is that a reissue application examination and an ex parte reexamination proceeding will not be conducted separately at the same time as to a particular patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids inconsistent or conflicting amendments and permits timely resolution. The decision whether to merge or stay is made in OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification responsibilities for concurrent proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner has responsibility to notify the Office of concurrent proceedings. File a Notification of Concurrent Proceedings (37 CFR 1.178(b) in reissue application; 37 CFR 1.565(a) or 1.985 in reexamination) as early as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If files are paper, hand-deliver them to OPLA when notifying via e-mail that proceedings are ready for consideration of merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for making decision on merging or staying proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision whether to merge the reissue application examination and the ex parte reexamination proceeding, or to stay one of the two proceedings, will not be made prior to the mailing of an order to reexamine the patent pursuant to 37 CFR 1.525. Determination on the request must be made within 3 months following the filing date of the request (35 U.S.C. 304 and 37 CFR 1.515).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is ordered, TC SPRE will await filing of any statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and any reply under 37 CFR 1.535 or the expiration of time for same, then promptly notify OPLA via e-mail that proceedings are ready for consideration of merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in deciding merge vs stay — status and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision is made case-by-case based upon the status of the various proceedings; due consideration will be given to the finality of the reexamination requested and the status of the reissue application examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue examination has not begun or a primary examiner rejection has not been appealed to the Board (37 CFR 41.31), OPLA likely will order a merger. If reissue application is on appeal to the Board or courts, that fact will be considered and may weigh against merger. If reissue examination has progressed such that merger is not desirable, reexamination generally will be stayed until reissue examination is complete on the issues then pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of reissue claims in reexamination — clean copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue claims used as the starting point in the reexamination proceeding must be presented in the reexamination proceeding as a “clean copy.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words bracketed in the reissue patent claim(s) would not appear in the reexamination clean copy; words added via the reissue patent appear in plain format in the reexamination clean copy (not italicized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action when reissue patent issues during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue patent issues on the patent under reexamination after reexamination is ordered, the next action from the examiner in the reexamination should point out that further proceedings in the reexamination will be based on the claims of the reissue patent and not on the patent surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 22.05 (Reexamination Based on Reissue Claims) may be used in the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for identical claims when merger ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a merger order requires that the patent owner place the same claims in the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, an amendment may be required to be filed within a specified time set in the order merging the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment to make the claims the same in each file is required but not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, paragraph 2, as being indefinite and failing to particularly point out the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of merged reissue application and reexamination proceeding — governing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application examination and a reexamination proceeding are merged, the merged examination will be conducted on the basis of the rules relating to the broader reissue application examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments should be submitted in accordance with reissue practice under 37 CFR 1.121(i) and 1.173; the examiner will apply reissue statute, rules, and case law to the merged proceeding. Each Office action will be a single action applying to both the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding and entered into both files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing responses in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any response by the applicant/patent owner in a merged proceeding must consist of a single response, filed in duplicate for entry in both files (or multiple copies if multiple reexamination proceedings are merged), and service of a copy must be made on any third party reexamination requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of all Office actions will be mailed to the third party reexamination requester but not to any other third party. If applicant fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action, the merged proceeding will be terminated and the reissue application will be held abandoned; a NIRC will be issued and the Director will proceed to issue a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 unless further action is clearly needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of express abandonment or CPA on merged proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant/patent owner files an express abandonment of the reissue application pursuant to 37 CFR 1.138, the next Office action will accept the express abandonment, dissolve the merged proceeding, and continue the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a continued prosecution reissue application (CPA) is filed and the existing reissue application is considered expressly abandoned, this will likely result in dissolution of the merged proceeding, a stay of the CPA, and separate continued prosecution of the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences after dissolution of merge based on abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the merged proceeding is dissolved based on abandonment of the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding continues, any grounds of rejection not applicable under reexamination should be withdrawn and any new grounds applicable under reexamination should be made by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any questions remaining which cannot be considered under reexamination following dissolution would be noted by the examiner as not being proper under reexamination pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c). There is no guarantee a continuation reissue application will be merged with the reexamination proceeding (it might be stayed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing an RCE of the reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant/patent owner files a request for continued examination (RCE) of the reissue application under 37 CFR 1.114, the reissue application is not considered to be expressly abandoned; rather the finality of the Office action is withdrawn, and the merged proceeding will continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE is not an abandonment of any application; merged proceedings thus continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to merge or stay — when to file and who may file
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge the reissue application and the reexamination proceeding, or stay one of them, should be filed before an order directing reexamination is issued because the Office will generally, sua sponte, make a decision to merge or stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions filed prior to determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) will be returned as premature and made of record in both files but no copy retained. Patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge or stay at the time the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 is filed or thereafter if Office has not acted. The requester (if not patent owner) may petition as part of reply under 37 CFR 1.535. Petitions by others are improper under 37 CFR 1.550(g) and will be returned. All merits decisions on such petitions are made in OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, extension of time fee, petition fee, appeal fee, brief fee, oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, only one fee need be paid for an appeal brief even though the brief relates to merged multiple proceedings and copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding. As to excess claim fees, reissue practice will control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling ex parte reexamination requests filed because of court-sanctioned agreements or stayed litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for ex parte reexamination which indicates it is filed as a result of an agreement by parties to litigation which agreement is sanctioned by a court, or that litigation is stayed for the filing of a reexamination request, will be taken up by the examiner for decision 6 weeks after the request was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination is ordered, the examination following the statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and reply under 37 CFR 1.535 will be expedited; Office actions will normally set a 1-month shortened statutory period for response (rather than 2 months). The 1-month period may be extended only upon a showing of sufficient cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Federal court decisions known at time of reexamination determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Federal Court decision on the merits of a patent is known to the examiner at the time the determination on the request for ex parte reexamination is made, the existence of a final court decision of claim validity does not necessarily mean that no new question is present because the Office uses different standards of proof and claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may accord deference to factual findings of the court where evidence is the same, but determination of whether a substantial new question of patentability exists will be made independently of the court’s decision. A non-final holding of claim invalidity or unenforceability will not be controlling. A final holding of claim invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) is controlling on the Office and a substantial new question would not be present as to those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for TC SPRE review when court decision known
rubrics_metrics.description: Any determination on a request for reexamination which the examiner makes after a Federal Court decision must be reviewed by the Technology Center (TC) Special Program Examiner (SPRE) to ensure that it conforms to the current Office litigation policy and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2240 for review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling reexamination ordered prior to Federal court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: When reexamination is ordered prior to a Federal Court decision, the determination on the request will be made within 3 months based on the record before the examiner without awaiting a court decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an ex parte reexamination is ordered, the reexamination will continue until the Office becomes aware that a court decision has issued; the patent owner is required by 37 CFR 1.565(a) to promptly notify the Office of any prior or concurrent proceeding or of any court decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Federal court decisions issued after reexamination ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reexamination is pending and a court decision issues (or Office becomes aware of a court decision), the order to reexamine is reviewed to see if a substantial new question of patentability is still present; if no substantial new question is present, the order to reexamine is vacated and reexamination is concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-final Federal Court decision concerning a patent under reexamination shall have no binding effect. The issuance of a final Federal Court decision upholding validity also will have no binding effect (Ethicon v. Quigg) because the Office uses a different standard of proof and may still find nonpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence. However, a final Federal Court holding of invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) is binding on the Office; claims held invalid/unenforceable will be withdrawn from consideration in the reexamination and the reexamination will be vacated if all claims were held invalid/unenforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph for claims held invalid by court (¶ 22.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 22.20 Claims Held Invalid By Court, No Longer Being Reexamined — 'Claims [1] of the [2] patent are not being reexamined in view of the final decision of [3]. Claim(s) [1] was/were held invalid/unenforceable by the [4].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in the Office action when claims are finally held invalid/unenforceable by the court and therefore are no longer subject to reexamination.
